official.deadline_note: The Doctoral School states the next application period for salaried positions is 24 August - 7 September 2026; the call is annual, so watch the Doctoral School page for the following window, which is not yet published.
official.application_cycle: Annual call held 24 August - 7 September 2026; positions start at the earliest on 1 January of the following year
official.status_note: The 2026 application period closed on 7 September 2026. The University states there is one application period each year covering all doctoral programmes, and the Studies Service instructions were last updated on 30 September 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The University of Helsinki does not collect tuition fees from doctoral researchers, and studies at the University are free.
benefits: Full-time salaried employment as a university-funded doctoral researcher, with the doctoral degree to be completed within four years
No tuition fees charged for doctoral research at the University of Helsinki
The same rights as other University employees: salary and social security, occupational health care, work facilities and equipment, and other staff services
Access to the University's research resources on the same basis as other researchers
eligibility: A qualifying Master's degree for doctoral studies
Eligibility to apply for the position as set out in the general and the doctoral-programme-specific instructions
Selection of one doctoral programme in the application form - the call covers all 14 doctoral programmes of the Doctoral School
An applicant may apply for only one university-funded doctoral researcher position in the call; where several applications are submitted, only the most recently dated one is reviewed
requirements: Contact a possible supervisor in advance and prepare the application together with that supervisor
Read both the general and the doctoral-programme-specific instructions before applying
Apply separately for the right to pursue a doctoral degree, since this call is only for funded positions
Submit the application in the language stated in the doctoral-programme-specific instructions
documents: Application submitted through the University's electronic recruitment system
Research plan prepared according to the programme-specific instructions
Attachments listed in the general and programme-specific instructions for the selected doctoral programme
Documentation of a qualifying Master's degree
selection_criteria: The doctoral programme steering group makes a proposal on the applicants to be selected for funded positions
The proposal goes to the unit director responsible for recruitment at the unit where the researcher would be employed, and that director decides on the employment
All employment contracts are placed within the faculties or independent institutes of the University
The list of awarded university-funded doctoral researcher positions is published on the Doctoral School's website
coverage: Salary from a full-time employment relationship with the University
Occupational health care, work facilities and other employee rights
application_method: Choose one doctoral programme and read its specific instructions in the Studies Service
Prepare the application, research plan and attachments together with a potential supervisor
Submit the single application through the University of Helsinki electronic recruitment system within the annual window
Apply for the doctoral study right separately in the doctoral programme's own call
official.application_route: One application per call through the University of Helsinki electronic recruitment system, choosing the doctoral programme that matches the research area; the programme steering group proposes and the recruiting unit director decides.
official.study_mode: Full-time work as a doctoral researcher
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction is published; the Doctoral School describes an international environment with one fourth of doctoral researchers being international students.
official.international_eligibility: Open to international applicants; completing a doctoral degree in English is possible in all doctoral programmes.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must select one of the 14 doctoral programmes of the University of Helsinki Doctoral School matching their research area; positions are allocated per doctoral programme.
official.research_requirement: A research plan prepared according to the doctoral-programme-specific instructions, and prior contact with a possible supervisor.
official.duration: Full-time employment; the doctoral degree should be completed within four years, and the employment contract sets its exact duration
official.description: The University of Helsinki Doctoral School allocates annual funding for doctoral researcher positions across all of the University's doctoral programmes. These are designated full-time positions as a university employment relationship, with the aim of completing a post-graduate doctoral degree within four years.

verification.notes: Read the Doctoral School positions page, the Studies Service instructions for the funded positions and the Doctoral School funding guidance. The salary figure is deliberately not published on these pages: the Studies Service states that information on the salary and further details of the employment relationship is in the call for applications, which was only open while the 24 August - 7 September 2026 window ran and is no longer accessible.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a salaried job, not a stipend, and it runs on a single annual window - 24 August to 7 September 2026 for positions starting at the earliest on 1 January. Two separate things must happen: you apply for the funded position here, and separately for the doctoral study right in your chosen programme's own call, which is easy to miss. Only one application per call is accepted, so your choice of doctoral programme is effectively final and must match your research area.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's graduates with a defined research topic who can secure a willing supervisor at the University of Helsinki before September and want an employment contract rather than a grant.
application_readiness_checklist: Pick the single doctoral programme that fits the research area - the application lets you choose only one
Email a potential supervisor early, since the instructions require you to prepare the application with them
Read both the general instructions and the programme-specific ones, including the language in which the application must be submitted
Prepare the research plan to the programme's specification rather than a generic outline
Diarise the separate doctoral study right call for the same programme, since this call funds only the position
common_rejection_risks: Assuming this call also grants the study right, which it does not
Submitting more than one application, after which only the most recently dated one is reviewed
A research plan that does not match the selected programme's requirements or the supervisor's capacity
Documents missing from the programme-specific attachment list, which varies between the 14 programmes
Applying in the wrong language, which is set per doctoral programme
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living and accommodation costs in Helsinki, research expenses beyond the resources normally open to University researchers (the Doctoral School and doctoral programmes do not generally cover these), and any special equipment or fee-based material the research requires.
document_audit: The attachment list differs per programme, so the general instructions alone are never sufficient
Only the most recently dated application is considered if more than one is submitted
The programme must be selected in the application form, and the dropdown lists doctoral programmes after the bachelor's and master's ones
Proof of a qualifying Master's degree is needed for doctoral eligibility
alerts: The 7 September 2026 deadline has passed; the call is annual but the next window is not yet published
Positions start at the earliest on 1 January of the following year, so budget for the preceding months
Contracts are placed within faculties or independent institutes, which may differ from the doctoral programme structure
Approximately a quarter of doctoral researchers work in an employment relationship, so competition across 14 programmes for university-funded posts is real
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Supervisor contact, one application plus attachments in the University's electronic recruitment system, a proposal from the doctoral programme steering group, then an employment decision by the recruiting unit director.
